question: Does Bat's public character wrapping split one Unicode ZWJ grapheme cluster across output rows because the printer wraps per scalar rather than per grapheme?

sources.name: sharkdp/bat
sources.claim: InteractivePrinter character and word wrapping iterate text.chars(), add per-scalar char_width values, and flush the current buffer when that scalar sum exceeds the row budget.

sources.name: sharkdp/bat CLI help
sources.claim: Public options expose --wrap=character and --terminal-width, allowing a deterministic narrow-width CLI probe.

command: GitHub Actions: Fieldwork Bat ZWJ wrap probe

dependencies: exact sharkdp/bat source fetched read-only at af59a3218303837421ce06bb2dc3c545525bba0f

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: At terminal width 2, 👩‍💻a keeps the complete 👩‍💻 grapheme on one row before wrapping a.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: The per-scalar source loop does not cause a user-visible cluster split in this path; stop this candidate.

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: At terminal width 2, 👩‍💻a breaks between ZWJ-linked scalars while the ordinary two-column control 界a wraps only between graphemes.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: Promote a target-executed grapheme-integrity wrapping candidate and map character/word modes separately.

stop_condition: Stop after the exact public CLI discriminator and one control classify grapheme integrity. Keep upstream read-only and require overlap refresh before any promotion.
